title: ErasureDeclared
description:
`erasure_declared` — an erasure declared: its kind, subject, request and manifest, the map of
every item it covers, and the holders who could read them. Projected into `kb_erasures`,
`kb_erasure_members`, `kb_erasure_former_holders` and, for an estate, `kb_erasure_estate_snapshots`.

The payload carries `erasure_id` because `_event_append` mints the event's own id and a payload
cannot name it. A map entry carries no status: an entry with `prior_erasure` and `prior_event`
is born `erased` (an earlier erasure already finished the item), and every other is born
`pending`.

`legacy` marks an erasure recorded from a door that names no erasure. A legacy declaration is
always of kind `resource` and carries no request, no manifest, no counts, no checksum and no
holders. Absent means false.

Erasure records are never redacted, and no key is a trail join key: an event is named by
`prior_event`, never `event_id`.

checksum.description:
The map's checksum (`erasure_map_checksum`): required for an estate, optional for any other
non-legacy erasure, and verified by the projector whenever present. Absent for a legacy
erasure.

counts.description: The declared member count per table, for an estate. Absent for a legacy erasure.

holders.description:
The profiles that held the erasure's items when it was declared. Empty for a legacy
erasure.

legacy.description: True for an erasure recorded from a door that names no erasure. Absent means false.

manifest_digest.description:
The sha256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical parsed erasure policy. Absent only when
`legacy`.

manifest_version.description:
The release semver of the erasure policy the erasure was declared under. Absent only when
`legacy`.

map.description: Every item the erasure covers when declared, containers before the leaves they hold.

request_ref.description: The declaring request's idempotency key. Absent only when `legacy`.

subject_id.description: The subject's id. Absent exactly when `subject_table` is.

subject_table.description:
The subject's table, as the DDL spells it: `kb_profiles` for an estate, `kb_resources` for
a resource or a block erasure. Absent for a selection.

ErasureKind.description:
What an erasure was declared over, as `kb_erasures.kind` spells it (its
`kb_erasures_kind_check`). Carried by `erasure_declared`.

oneOf.description: A person's estate; the subject is a profile.
One resource; the subject is the resource. Every legacy erasure is of this kind.
A selection of items; there is no subject.
A resource's block history; the subject is the resource.

ErasureMapEntry.description: One item of an erasure's map, as `erasure_declared` declares it.

parent.description: The container member (a context or a cogmap) of the same erasure that holds this item.

prior_erasure.description:
The earlier erasure that already finished this item. Present with `prior_event`, and the
row is then born `erased`.

prior_event.description: The event that erased this item in the earlier erasure.

ErasureMemberRef.description: An item an erasure member names: its table, as the DDL spells it, and its id.

ErasureMemberTable.description:
A table whose rows an erasure member can name. Serializes as the DDL spells the table.
Ordered by declaration, so it can key a map that serializes with stable bytes.
